short: The cavalry charge that stopped Ottoman expansion into central Europe.
full:
An Ottoman army under Grand Vizier Kara Mustafa Pasha reached Vienna on 14 July 1683 and began mining its walls. A garrison of about 15,000 under Ernst Rudiger von Starhemberg held for two months while the defences were breached section by section and the city ran short of food. A relief army assembled under the Holy Roman Empire and the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, commanded by King Jan III Sobieski.

On 12 September the relief force attacked down the wooded slopes of the Kahlenberg. In the late afternoon Sobieski committed the cavalry, some 18,000 horse led by around 3,000 Polish winged hussars, in what is usually described as the largest cavalry charge in history. The Ottoman camp broke within hours and Kara Mustafa was executed at Belgrade that December. The battle opened a Habsburg counter-offensive that took all of Hungary by 1699 and ended Ottoman expansion in central Europe. Sabaton's "Winged Hussars", from The Last Stand (2016), is about the charge.
